extracted.intended_audience: artists, architects, art-historians, and students of medieval/Venetian church ornament and architectural decoration
extracted.subtask_description: Guiding principles and evaluative criteria for designing, assessing, or reproducing early Venetian (Murano) church architecture and ornament — focusing on proportion, material, colour, and ornament treatment. Includes practical examples (apse bands, archivolt, capitals, inlaid triangles) showing how these principles are applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportional harmony (arithmetical ratios)
rubrics_metrics.description: The relations of architectural distances and widths should follow deliberate arithmetic proportions (e.g., interval of shafts : width of aisle : width of transept : width of nave = 8'2" : 16'4" : 24'6" : 32'8"). Such numeric relations produce a perception of harmony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure and arrange major elements so their spans relate by simple ratios; the author treats these proportions as evidence of a 'true love of harmony' and a fundamental principle of early Venetian design. See the apse and nave measurements as worked examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliberate subtle variation within repeating motifs
rubrics_metrics.description: Repetition should not be monotonous; repeated elements (e.g., trefoils) are 'hardly ever twice of the same size' and are varied purposefully so that the same leaf is 'continually repeated, but never twice of the same size.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce small, purposeful changes of scale/shape within repeating patterns to mimic natural growth and sustain visual interest — measure variations so they appear intentional rather than accidental.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of colour as a primary organising principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Colour is of highest importance; the eye should be drawn as much to the chequers of the stone as to the intricacies of chiselling. Colour placement emphasises centres and hierarchies (e.g., the black-and-white marble emphasises the centre of the chain).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan colour contrasts (white, purple, red, green, black marbles; yellow and red bricks) to create focal points, balance, and subordinate/primary bands. Use darker or contrasting pieces to mark centres or important junctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate treatment of sculpture relative to material colour
rubrics_metrics.description: Sculpture and carving must be matched to the material's colour: 'the purple capitals are all left plain; the white are all sculptured.' Carving coloured stones can adulterate their hue by producing shadow and drawing attention away from the colour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid deep carving on richly coloured stones; if ornament is needed on a coloured stone, employ light incisions or etched outlines to indicate finish without destroying surface colour. Reserve full relief work for pale/white stones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale of relief and modelling tuned to viewing distance
rubrics_metrics.description: Ornament should be executed in relief appropriate to the usual viewing distance ('thrown out in low and flat relief' so elements are visible at 17 or 18 feet).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust depth and boldness of carving so motifs read clearly from where observers will stand; use low shallow relief with dark ground to preserve crispness at distance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hierarchy and contrast between decorative courses
rubrics_metrics.description: Different horizontal courses (bands) should have distinct characters and visual weights so they do not merely imitate each other; the lower band is richer and more central while the upper is lighter and subordinated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vary height, richness of material, and pattern density between bands (e.g., lower band uses variegated marbles and finer chiselling; upper band uses brick and bolder patterns) so the parts form a harmonious whole with clear hierarchy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intentional balancing across complex compositions
rubrics_metrics.description: Groupings and placements are planned so opposite sides 'answer each other' even when both cannot be seen at once; apparent local imbalances are countered by balancing elements elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When arranging repeat groups or decorative clusters, consider the whole elevation/apse plan and create reciprocal arrangements that balance the composition globally, not only locally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using contrast to turn awkward constraints into features
rubrics_metrics.description: Where pattern must meet difficult geometry or awkward spaces (e.g., where a band is broken by higher arches), the mediæval artist 'directed the eye to the difficulty' by making that part conspicuous (e.g., using reversed triangles, contrasting stones).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rather than conceal joints/interruptions, design them as emphatic features with contrasting colour, shape, or ornament so they read as intentional solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material selection informed by function and appearance
rubrics_metrics.description: Use stronger materials for structural parts (yellow brick for strength) and more variegated/precious marbles for decoration; materials were 'cast into any shape and size' to suit arches and tiles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose materials with appropriate mechanical and visual properties: durable masonry where load is required, varied coloured marbles for inlaid ornament, and manufacture/custom-shape elements where needed to fit patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precise modular arrangement of inlaid pieces to emphasise centres
rubrics_metrics.description: Inlaid triangular stones are grouped so that particular pieces (e.g., a black-and-white marble) emphasise the centre of a chain 'exactly as a painter would use a dark touch.' Group sizes and counts are adjusted to the width of each side so centres align.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan modular ornament counts (how many triangles per side, which kinds) to create centre emphasis and mirrored order along curved or faceted surfaces; adjust group composition where sides differ in width.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy of ornament: match intricacy to material and context
rubrics_metrics.description: Where materials are coarse or dark, use bolder patterns; where fine variegated marbles occur, use finer chiselling. The workman 'made his chiselling finer where it was to go with the variegated marbles, and used a bolder pattern with the coarser brick and dark stone.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scale the intricacy of carving to the richness and scale of the material so ornament complements rather than competes with the substrate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliberate geometric adjustment to maintain visual harmony
rubrics_metrics.description: Geometric differences introduced by construction (e.g., upper band projecting so sides are broader above than below) should be compensated by changing motif proportions (making upper triangles higher and more acute or narrowing bases) to preserve a harmonious whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where projection or cornices change the apparent width/height of bands, alter motif dimensions (height, base width) deliberately so the courses read as unified rather than accidentally mismatched.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis by selective preservation or loss (honesty of fragments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fragments and differences (e.g., some marbles fallen away) reveal original priorities: preserved pieces often indicate intended colour and emphasis. The author infers original schemes from remaining fragments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When restoring or assessing historic ornament, read surviving elements as indicators of original emphasis and use them to guide conservation or reproduction choices rather than inventing uniformly new ornament.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of simple repeating motifs (trefoil) for enduring delight
rubrics_metrics.description: Simple motifs like the trefoil, repeated many times yet varied, afford lasting pleasure because they combine 'the love of trinity in unity' with 'the sense of fulness with order.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor archetypal, rhythmically repeated forms that can be varied subtly; ensure they fill spaces with propriety and avoid crowding or awkward gaps.
